description:
NVIDIA is looking for an AI Factory Infrastructure Engineer to join its Infrastructure Specialists team. Interested in finding system issues before they slow validation? Excited by the challenge of keeping large-scale Linux, SLURM, and GPU systems operating smoothly? This role works across Linux HPC / AI clusters, SLURM services, GPU infrastructure, and operational tooling that support large-scale AI and high-performance computing. We are looking for strong systems troubleshooting, sound operational judgment, and a practical approach to improving system health during deployment and validation.
 
 What you'll be doing: 
 Check system health before validation by verifying node readiness, scheduler health, GPU availability, and critical cluster services. 
 Support stable operation during validation by troubleshooting Linux, SLURM, GPU, network, and storage issues and by partnering with the right teams to restore healthy system behavior. 
 Separate infrastructure faults from workload or test issues and turn findings into clear next steps, remediation actions, and operational guidance. 
 Improve recurring issues through better diagnostics, runbooks, alerts, and targeted automation that reduces manual effort and helps teams respond more efficiently.
 
 What we need to see: 
 BS or MS degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer information systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience. 
 5+ years of experience in site reliability engineering, infrastructure engineering, systems engineering, or production operations in large-scale Linux bare-metal HPC cluster environments. 
 Strong Linux administration and troubleshooting skills across services, processes, networking, storage, resource contention, and system performance. 
 Experience with installing, operating or troubleshooting bare-metal HPC clusters, including SLURM or other workload managers, network provisioning services and node health monitoring.  
 Practical Python or Bash scripting skills and familiarity with Ansible or similar tools for operational tasks. 
 Experience with monitoring, telemetry, logs, dashboards, alerts, or diagnostic tooling such as Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, or similar platforms. 
 Demonstrated troubleshooting and remediation experience, including the ability to investigate failures, identify root causes, and restore healthy system behavior. 
 
 
 Ways to stand out from the crowd: 
 Experience with GPU telemetry, NVIDIA DCGM, and SLURM metrics. 
 Experience with NVIDIA Base Command Manager or similar bare-metal cluster management platforms. 
 Practical knowledge of bare-metal provisioning, InfiniBand, RoCE, NVLink or NVSwitch, and parallel storage failure modes. 
 Experience supporting early-life cluster operations, system validation, or customer deployment environments. 
 Background with containerized applications and workloads. (Docker, Singularity, Kubernetes, Pyxis, Enroot) 
 
 NVIDIA is widely considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. Some of the world's most forward-thinking and hardworking people are working for us. If you're creative and autonomous, we want to hear from you. 
 
 
Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and other objective job-related factors. The expected base salary range for this position is 157,500 USD – 299,000 USD. 
 You will also be eligible for equity and benefits . 
 







Applications for this job will be accepted at least until November 30, 2026. 
 This posting is for an existing vacancy. 
 NVIDIA uses AI tools in its recruiting processes.
 
NVIDIA is committed to fostering an inclusive work environment and proud to be an equal opportunity employer. As we highly value diversity in our current and future employees, we do not discriminate (including in our hiring and promotion practices) on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability status or any other characteristic protected by law.
